title: introduce-ci-dependency-bucketing-and-lightweight-presubmit-prober
author: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Our presubmit pipeline has grown heavy as we accumulate transient devdeps and broad lint/test coverage. This PR introduces a small, low-risk refactor that: (1) partitions CI-facing dependencies into stable and ephemeral buckets to reduce install churn, and (2) adds a lightweight presubmit prober that runs a curated set of end-to-end smoke checks (including a few representative LLM prompts against the OpenAPI-compatible inference API) to detect regressions in streaming/structured-output behavior before full integration tests run. Motivation: reduce CI setup time, limit noisy dependency churn, and catch API contract regressions earlier with a cheap smoke stage. What this changes: - CI dep bucketing: a new ci/deps/manifest.yaml describes two groups: stable (pinned semver, cached) and ephemeral (fast-refresh, optional). The presubmit image build uses the manifest to only install ephemeral deps when changed. - Presubmit prober: a thin Go binary (ci/presubmit/prober/main.go) that loads a small prompt set (ci/presubmit/prompts/*.jsonl) and runs lightweight checks (tokenization sanity, streaming frames received, basic structured JSON validation). It returns non-zero only for clear contract breaks. - Staged presubmit lanes: workflow now has quick-lint -> prober -> full-integration gates. The prober gate is short (<= 30s on average) and can be toggled via labels. Migration and rollout: default opt-in for repos under redwood/; rollout plan included in the checklist below. Rollback: revert workflow YAML or label toggle to disable prober immediately. Risks: false positives for model output are mitigated by using deterministic synthetic prompts and schema checks only. Implementation notes: - Added caching key changes to workflows to include bucket manifest checksum so caches are invalidated only when stable bucket changes. - Adjusted lint runner to skip heavy linters in the quick-lint lane and surface them in the slower lanes. - CI images updated to include a minimal runtime for the prober (Go1.21, small curl shim). Checklist: - [x] Add ci/deps/manifest.yaml and install harness - [x] Implement presubmit prober and sample prompt set - [x] Wire prober into .github/workflows/presubmit.yml as a staged check - [x] Add doc snippet to docs/contrib/ci.md describing bucketing TTLs - [x] Run in canary mode on redwood/* and redwood-sdk-* for 72h before org-wide rollout Related work: Linear ENG-4022, ENG-4098. This description contains the end-to-end context, migration notes, and rollback plan.

Also request that the prompt set be clearly labeled synthetic vs production so we don't accidentally leak customer prompts. - Aisha: updated main.go to limit concurrency via --workers flag and added metadata fields to prompts. Pushed commit a6e4d21.

Miguel Santos: Suggest adding an explicit cache key tie to ci/deps/manifest.yaml checksum to avoid invalidating cache on unrelated changes. - Aisha: implemented cache_key_util and adjusted workflow, see f14b0d2.
Ben Walker (approval): Verified canary run results and infra metrics. Approve after CI green and a short observation window.
release_notes: Introduce dependency bucketing for CI and a lightweight presubmit prober that runs schema/smoke checks on a small representative prompt set. This reduces presubmit latency and catches contract regressions early. Backwards compatible: prober is opt-in via labels during canary, and bucketing is transparent to dev workflows.
notes_for_ops: Ops: when deploying org-wide, watch cache-hit ratio and presubmit queue depth. If presubmit_prober begins to fail due to infra slowness, disable by adding label 'prober-disable' to the workflow_dispatch or revert .github/workflows/presubmit.yml. The manifest checksum (ci/deps/manifest.yaml) is used in cache keys; rotating stable bucket should be done with a follow-up PR that notes cache invalidation.
testing_and_metrics: Canary run: 72h across redwood/redwood, redwood-sdk-python, redwood-sdk-typescript. Observed median presubmit setup time reduced 28% (from 86s to 62s) on canary projects. Cache hit rate for stable bucket ~94% across canary. Prober false-positive rate: 0/48 synthetic checks; one flaky network failure on test runner was mitigated by retry logic. Metrics tracked in Console: ci.presubmit.setup_ms, ci.prober.duration_ms, ci.cache.hit_ratio.
migration_steps: 1) Merge to main behind 'canary' label. 2) Monitor canary for 72h. 3) Expand label targeting to more repos. 4) After 1 week, flip default to enabled org-wide and deprecate old heavy quick-presubmit job. See docs/contrib/ci.md for TTL knobs.
